name: Nearby places: nearest-N and within-radius search by category
description: List places from a local places dataset around a centre point, nearest first (WGS-84 ellipsoidal distance in whole metres), optionally limited to a radius, categories (Turkish or English words such as eczane, kafe, banka, iskele) and a name fragment; or count which categories exist around a point. Answers "bu noktaya 1 km içindeki eczaneler" and "en yakın 3 kafe".

provenance.license_check: GitHub API license field: MIT, matching the actual license file
provenance.metadata_source: public GitHub repository API (license field and created_at), observed this round; actual license file inspected
provenance.reference_values: Fixture places are synthetic (CC0). Expected result lists, distances and counts were generated by reference/upstream_harness.js, which loads the same fixture file directly and calls pinned upstream geolib.orderByDistance in Node; the harness re-implements the documented filters independently of the Python port.

dataset.description: Dataset name (no folders), e.g. demo_kadikoy or my_pois.csv

budget.enforcement: Raw CLI byte limit and POSIX alarm; strict schema, finite values and nesting checks; MCP subprocess killed/reaped after 10 seconds. One active calculation. Not a hostile-code sandbox.

data.reads: local files by dataset name from SKILLPACK_MAP_DATA or ../map_data

mcp.instructions: Local offline map tool. The dataset is a file NAME inside the folder the user configured (SKILLPACK_MAP_DATA); never invent coordinates or names. Results come from the local data and code; explain them, state data limits (no live traffic) and ask the human to confirm before acting on them. Credit OpenStreetMap contributors when showing OSM-derived data.

limitations: Straight-line distance on the WGS-84 ellipsoid (Vincenty, rounded to whole metres as upstream orderByDistance does), not walking or driving distance; use M031 matrix for road times. The radius test is inclusive (distance <= radius_m). Category words are mapped through a small fixed Turkish/English alias table (shown in categories_used); unknown words are matched literally against the dataset category. Opening hours are copied from the data and never evaluated, so "open now" questions cannot be answered. Results depend entirely on what the local dataset contains.
port_notes: Ports geolib v2.0.24 getDistance (Vincenty inverse with toFixed(precision) then Math.round, elevation ignored, NaN for non-convergence turned into an error) and orderByDistance (distance per place, stable ascending sort). With default accuracy 1 and precision 0 distances are whole metres; ties keep dataset order. Filtering by radius, categories, name and the alias table are Skillpack rules. Note: geolib getRhumbLineBearing/getBearing are deliberately not used (their source comment cites GPL-licensed material).
